I don’t think it’s honest to pretend like this would just be a standalone plan, either. Attacking Russian airports would place further strain on the Russian economy. The Russian aviation sector is already facing financial difficulties. It would be happening now, amidst a wider attack on Russia’s economy which can be seen with refineries and Wildberries. But, as noted, there’s a real risk of collateral damage in attacking airports primarily used by civilians, as well as a PR hit. Even if you’re just trying to hit radar or fuel sites, drones getting shot down, jammed or just plain missing could hit passenger liners or a terminal. Not to mention that any horrible accidents seeing a plane shot down or crash would be blamed on Ukraine. This collateral risk, and the consequences, has likely driven the consideration on carrying out the campaign. A key point though: Ukraine’s civilian airports have been out of action for four years now. This would be reciprocal. A further demonstration that everything can be reciprocated. A Russian response is always factored into these decisions. It’s not about a single action leading to a capitulation, it’s about showing to the Russians that everything they’ve done to Ukraine can be done to Russia. THAT drives unease.

RT by @hey_itsmyturn: Four commanders in Hamas's elite Nukhba Force were killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City yesterday, the military announces. Palestinian media reported that the strike on a cafe near the city's port killed six and wounded 14. The IDF says it was able to confirm that the strike killed four Nukhba Force commanders in Hamas's Beit Lahia Battalion. They are named as: Muhammad Hamdi Ahmed al-Masri, a company commander; Samad Samir Harb Abu Jabal, a platoon commander who invaded Israel during the October 7 onslaught; Muhammad Attar, a platoon commander; and Muhammad Fathi Hussein Nasser, also a platoon commander. The military says the operatives were involved in advancing attacks on troops. "The commanders' activities posed a threat to IDF troops, and they were therefore eliminated in an aerial strike to remove the threat," the army adds.
